prompt: Alexander the Great takes the island city of Tyre
fact: The siege lasted about seven months.

prompt: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Roman Beirut (Berytus)
fact: Berytus was home to one of the Roman Empire's best-known law schools.

prompt: Crusaders capture Tripoli after a long siege
fact: Baldwin I, king of Jerusalem, played a leading role in the capture.

prompt: Crusader king Baldwin I captures Beirut
fact: He took the city in May, with the help of a Genoese fleet.

prompt: Saladin retakes Beirut from the Crusaders
fact: It came in the same campaign in which he took most of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

prompt: The Mamluk sultan Qalawun takes Tripoli from the Crusaders
fact: He broke his truce with the Crusaders to take the fortified port.

prompt: The Ottomans defeat the Mamluks at Marj Dabiq, opening the way to Lebanon
fact: The battle was fought on 24 August, north of Aleppo.

prompt: The first book printed in the Middle East comes off a press at the Qozhaya monastery
fact: It was a psalter, printed in Syriac script.

prompt: Emir Fakhr al-Din II is executed in Istanbul
fact: He was captured the year before, after decades ruling much of today's Lebanon.

prompt: The Battle of Ain Dara reshapes power in Mount Lebanon
fact: The Qaysi faction defeated its Yamani rivals.

prompt: An American missionary rediscovers the lower galleries of Jeita Grotto
fact: The missionary was Reverend William Thomson.

prompt: Khalil al-Khoury launches the Beirut newspaper Hadiqat al-Akhbar
fact: The first issue came out on 1 January.

prompt: Mount Lebanon becomes a special Ottoman district, the Mutasarrifate
fact: It lasted until the end of Ottoman rule in 1918.

prompt: The Syrian Protestant College, today's American University of Beirut, holds its first classes
fact: It started with 16 students; it took the name AUB in 1920.

prompt: The Jesuits found Saint Joseph University in Beirut
fact: It came nine years after the Syrian Protestant College, Beirut's first university.

prompt: Gibran Khalil Gibran is born in Bsharri
fact: He was born on 6 January.

prompt: Ottoman authorities hang nationalists in Beirut's Burj Square, later renamed Martyrs' Square
fact: Lebanon marks the day, 6 May, as Martyrs' Day.

prompt: General Gouraud proclaims the State of Greater Lebanon
fact: He spoke from the steps of the Pine Residence in Beirut on 1 September.

prompt: Wadih El Safi, the 'Voice of Lebanon', is born in Niha
fact: Niha is a village in the Shouf.

prompt: Gibran publishes The Prophet in the United States
fact: He wrote it in English.

prompt: Charles Debbas becomes the first president of the Lebanese Republic
fact: He was re-elected in 1929.

prompt: Sabah, the 'Empress of Lebanese song', is born in Bdadoun
fact: She was born on 10 November.

prompt: The newspaper An-Nahar is founded in Beirut
fact: L'Orient was founded the same year.

prompt: The National Museum of Beirut opens
fact: Head of state Alfred Naccache opened it on 27 May.

prompt: Lebanon becomes independent
fact: Independence followed the French arrest and release of President Bechara El Khoury and other leaders.

prompt: Lebanon is one of seven founding members of the Arab League
fact: The league was founded on 22 March.

prompt: Middle East Airlines is founded
fact: The airline still flies from Beirut today.

prompt: Mikhail Naimy publishes The Book of Mirdad
fact: It was first published in Lebanon.

prompt: Amin Maalouf is born in Beirut
fact: He was born on 25 February.

prompt: Lebanon wins its first Olympic medals, both in wrestling
fact: Zakaria Chihab took silver and Khalil Taha bronze, in Greco-Roman wrestling at Helsinki.

prompt: A decree gives Lebanese women the right to vote
fact: At first it covered women with primary education; women first voted the following year.

prompt: Beirut's new international airport opens at Khalde
fact: It opened on 12 April, and the old airfield was demolished soon after.

prompt: Ziad Rahbani, son of Fairuz and Assi Rahbani, is born
fact: He was born on 1 January, in Antelias.

prompt: Fairuz gives her first performance at the Baalbeck festival
fact: She performed there with the Rahbani brothers.

prompt: Speleologists discover the upper galleries of Jeita Grotto
fact: The lower galleries opened to visitors the same year.

prompt: Lebanese television starts broadcasting
fact: The first programmes went out on 28 May.

prompt: The Casino du Liban opens
fact: It opened in December.

prompt: Myrna Bustani becomes the first woman in Lebanon's parliament
fact: She was elected to finish her late father Emile Bustani's term.

prompt: Intra Bank collapses after a run on its deposits
fact: The trouble became public in early October.

prompt: Amin Maalouf publishes The Crusades Through Arab Eyes
fact: It first came out in French, as Les Croisades vues par les Arabes.

prompt: Amin Maalouf wins the Prix Goncourt for Le Rocher de Tanios
fact: The Goncourt is France's best-known literary prize.

prompt: Lebanon hosts the AFC Asian Cup for the first time
fact: Japan won the final 1-0 against Saudi Arabia.

prompt: Lebanon plays its first basketball World Championship
fact: It has qualified three more times since.

prompt: The first Beirut Marathon is run
fact: It was founded by May El Khalil.

prompt: Nadine Labaki's film Caramel premieres at Cannes
fact: It screened in the Directors' Fortnight section.

prompt: Beirut is UNESCO's World Book Capital
fact: The same year, Beirut hosted the Jeux de la Francophonie.

prompt: Amin Maalouf is elected to the Académie française
fact: He took the seat once held by Claude Lévi-Strauss.

prompt: Ziad Doueiri's The Insult gives Lebanon its first Oscar nomination
fact: It was nominated for best foreign-language film.

prompt: Nadine Labaki's Capernaum wins the Jury Prize at Cannes
fact: The next year it became Lebanon's second Oscar nominee.

prompt: Amin Maalouf becomes perpetual secretary of the Académie française
fact: He succeeded Hélène Carrère d'Encausse.

prompt: Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany visits the ruins of Baalbek
fact: German archaeologists started digging there soon after his visit.

prompt: Lebanon adopts its national anthem, Koullouna lil watan
fact: Words by Rachid Nakhlé, music by Wadih Sabra, both picked through public contests.

prompt: Lebanon holds its last official census
fact: Every population figure since then has been an estimate.

prompt: Etel Adnan, poet and painter, is born in Beirut
fact: She wrote in French and English, and painted for most of her life.

prompt: Marcel Khalife, oud player and composer, is born in Amchit
fact: He was born on 10 June.

prompt: Majida El Roumi is born in Kfarshima
fact: Kfarshima is a village just south of Beirut.

prompt: A deadly earthquake strikes the Chouf and the south
fact: It struck on the morning of 16 March, centred on the village of Chehim.

prompt: The Sursock Museum opens in Achrafieh
fact: Nicolas Sursock had left his villa to the city as an art museum.

prompt: The Banque du Liban, Lebanon's central bank, starts operating
fact: It opened its doors on 1 April, a few months after the law that created it.

prompt: Georgina Rizk is crowned Miss Universe
fact: She was the first Lebanese and the first Arab woman to win the title.

prompt: Fairuz releases the album Wahdon, composed by her son Ziad
fact: Ziad Rahbani produced it, and composed and arranged the songs.

prompt: Fairuz releases the album Kifak Inta
fact: Its title song was written and composed by Ziad Rahbani.

prompt: Maroun Bagdadi's Out of Life wins the Jury Prize at Cannes
fact: The film follows a French photographer taken hostage in Beirut.

prompt: The Baalbeck International Festival returns after the war
fact: It had been suspended since the start of the civil war.

prompt: Ziad Doueiri's film West Beyrouth is released
fact: At Cannes it screened in the Directors' Fortnight.

prompt: Elias Khoury publishes his novel Gate of the Sun
fact: It first came out in Arabic, in Beirut, as Bab al-Shams.

prompt: Beirut is the Arab Capital of Culture
fact: Cairo held the title first, three years earlier.

prompt: Charles Elachi, future head of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, is born in Rayak
fact: He was born on 18 April.

prompt: Lebanese-born Charles Elachi becomes director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory
fact: He led it for fifteen years, until 2016.

prompt: Women join a Lebanese cabinet for the first time
fact: Leila Solh became minister of industry and Wafaa Hamza a minister of state.

prompt: Rima Fakih, born in Srifa, is crowned Miss USA
fact: She moved to the United States as a baby.

prompt: Lebanon earns a place at the Asian Cup through qualifying for the first time
fact: Its only earlier Asian Cup was as host, in 2000.

prompt: Hoda Barakat wins the International Prize for Arabic Fiction
fact: She won for her novel The Night Mail.

prompt: Lebanon loses the basketball Asia Cup final to Australia by two points
fact: The final in Jakarta ended 75-73.

prompt: Nancy Ajram is born in Achrafieh
fact: She was born on 16 May.

prompt: Nadine Labaki is born in Baabdat
fact: She was born on 18 February.

prompt: Butrus al-Bustani gives a public lecture arguing that women should be educated
fact: He later began the first volumes of an Arabic encyclopedia.

prompt: Butrus al-Bustani launches the magazine Al-Jinan
fact: He was one of the leading figures of the Arab literary revival.

prompt: Butrus al-Bustani, scholar and encyclopedist, is born
fact: He died in Beirut while still working on his encyclopedia.

prompt: Jurji Zaydan, historian and novelist, is born in Beirut
fact: He made his career in Egypt.

prompt: Jurji Zaydan founds the magazine Al-Hilal in Cairo
fact: It was his own journal, and he edited it until his death.

prompt: Ameen Rihani is born in Freike
fact: He died in the same village.

prompt: Ameen Rihani publishes The Book of Khalid
fact: It is described as the first Arab-American novel written in English; Gibran drew its illustrations.

prompt: May Ziadeh, who later ran a famous literary salon in Cairo, is born
fact: She was born in Nazareth to a Lebanese father.

prompt: The painter Moustafa Farroukh is born
fact: He later taught art at the American University of Beirut.

prompt: Assi Rahbani is born in Antelias
fact: He and his brother Mansour began as police officers in Beirut.

prompt: Mansour Rahbani is born in Antelias
fact: He kept writing musical plays after his brother Assi died.

prompt: Elia Abu Madi founds the Arabic magazine Al-Samir in New York
fact: It later became a newspaper.

prompt: Ghassan Tueni is born
fact: He became editor of An-Nahar in his early twenties.

prompt: Ghassan Tueni takes over An-Nahar after his father's death
fact: He was jailed more than once for what he wrote.

prompt: Khayreddine al-Ahdab becomes the first Muslim to head a Lebanese government
fact: He had been a journalist, and founded the newspaper al-Ahd al-Jadid.

prompt: Rashid Karami becomes prime minister at 34, the youngest ever
fact: He went on to hold the post more often than anyone.

prompt: Suleiman Frangieh is elected president by a single vote
fact: The vote in parliament was 50 to 49.

prompt: Nadia Tueni, who wrote in French, is born in Beirut
fact: She married Ghassan Tueni of An-Nahar.

prompt: Nadia Tueni wins the Académie française's poetry prize
fact: The prize was for her collection Poèmes pour une histoire.

prompt: Filmmaker Jocelyne Saab is born in Beirut
fact: She started out as a war reporter.

prompt: Jocelyne Saab makes Beirut, Never Again with the writer Etel Adnan
fact: She spent the civil war filming her own city.

prompt: Myrna Bustani founds the Al Bustan Festival
fact: Thirty years earlier she had become the first woman in parliament.

prompt: Habib Pacha Saad becomes president of the Lebanese Republic
fact: He had already been Speaker of Parliament and prime minister.
